sk.overview: Powerica operates across two industries: (1) India's standby power / diesel-generator (DG set) market, where DG sets, UPS, inverters and battery storage provide backup power during outages/voltage fluctuations across commercial, manufacturing, IT/data-centre, telecom and infrastructure sectors (F&S Report); and (2) India's wind power sector within the broader renewable energy industry, where wind plays a pivotal role in the country's energy transition (CRISIL Report).

currentContext.strengths: customer lock-in: long-term contracted green ammonia offtake — evidence: signed a 10-year binding Green Ammonia Purchase Agreement (GAPA) with SECI for 60,000 TPA valued at ~₹3,135 crore [planned]|licence/regulatory: grid access in a grid-constrained industry — evidence: the Company expanded its Open Access grid connectivity across Rajasthan, Haryana, and Tamil Nadu, while the MD&A names grid connectivity and renewable energy evacuation as industry execution challenges
currentContext.strategies: Flywheel model: develop high-quality, bankable assets, selectively monetise them to recycle capital, strengthen the balance sheet and redeploy capital into new opportunities.|Move from Generation alone to an integrated Generation, Storage and Consumption platform, cross-selling solar, storage and later green hydrogen derivatives to existing customers to build recurring, multi-product business.|Scale BESS across C&I hybrid projects, the merchant market and utility-scale storage through disciplined project selection.|Build a Consumption business in green hydrogen, green ammonia and green methanol, and participate in end-use sectors such as data centres with generation and storage at the back end.|Early-mover positioning in floating solar and agrivoltaic installations to address land availability constraints.|Expand internationally: presence established in Africa and Latin America through EPC and development projects, now seeking a BESS foothold in these regions; exploring renewable projects in Alberta, Canada.|Remain open to strategic mergers and acquisitions (asset, project and corporate) where aligned with the vision.|Use AI-enabled monitoring and digitised site-level financial tracking so that overheads do not rise in step with project count.|Execution with the right profitability and disciplined capital allocation.
currentContext.expansion: Generation: in FY26 the company secured one of the world's largest floating solar installations at Maithon Dam, Jharkhand; commissioned its first ISTS-connected solar project at Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh; commissioned Goa's largest project under VNM; secured its first STU-connected utility-scale solar project in Gujarat and an integrated ground-mounted and carport solar project at an international airport in Kerala; and entered Latin America with a solar project at an international airport in Guyana. It secured ~4,780 acres of land and expanded open-access grid connectivity across Rajasthan, Haryana and Tamil Nadu, with 700+ MW under execution and 2,500+ MW in the pipeline. Storage: secured its first utility-scale 100 MW Solar + 50 MW/300 MWh BESS project connected to the Central Transmission Utility, commissioned the first Group Captive Open Access Solar + BESS hybrid project in Rajasthan, and has 1,000+ MWh of BESS under execution and a 3,000+ MWh development pipeline, helped by ~₹150 crore of Viability Gap Funding. Consumption: a 10-year binding green ammonia offtake with SECI for 60,000 TPA, 10,000 MTPA of green hydrogen allocated, 1,200+ acres identified in Madhya Pradesh for the green ammonia project, green fuels projects advancing across Madhya Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh, and continuing compressed biogas development. Vision 2030 targets over 6 GW of EPC capacity, more than 2.5 GW of IPP assets and 20 GWh of battery storage capacity.
currentContext.mdna: The energy transition is moving from capacity addition to reliability; government tenders, utility requirements and customer expectations are increasingly shaped around integrated renewable solutions with BESS playing a central role.|Management expects the BESS business to become an increasingly significant revenue contributor from FY27 onwards.|India's energy storage requirement is expected to rise sharply as renewable capacity scales, making BESS central to a flexible and resilient power system.|Demand environment and customer interest across renewable energy, storage and green fuels (green ammonia, green methanol) described as robust.|Pradhan Mantri Surya Sarovar Yojana (PM-SSY) brings policy focus to floating solar integrated with storage, supporting the floating solar direction.|Land availability is one of the industry's biggest constraints; floating and agrivoltaic solar are the company's response.|Industry execution headwinds: transmission infrastructure, grid connectivity, evacuation, land acquisition and Right of Way, plus commodity, currency and equipment price volatility adding procurement and project cost pressure.|Green ammonia steps are calibrated to offtake viability and policy clarity in a highly regulated sector.|Solar: 835+ MW cumulative delivered, 700+ MW under execution and 2,500+ MW (more than 2.5 GWp) in the pipeline.|BESS: 1,000+ MWh of projects under execution and 3,000+ MWh in the pipeline; BESPA agreements signed for 550 MWh across Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and a Navratna PSU.|Won over 190 MWh of C&I hybrid (solar + BESS) orders and secured the first utility-scale solar-plus-BESS hybrid project.|Secured a 234 MW floating solar project in Jharkhand (Maithon Dam) with a major public-sector power utility, described as the state's largest floating solar project.|10-year binding Green Ammonia Purchase Agreement with SECI for 60,000 TPA under the National Green Hydrogen Mission.|Order pipeline described as healthy.
